newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN SHARES UP AT NOON ON CHANG'AN GAINS.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN SHARES UP AT NOON ON CHANG'AN GAINS.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index rose at midday on Monday, powered by sharp gains by Chongqing Chang'an 2625.SZ, brokers said.
The index gained 1.98 points or 1.51 percent to 133.46 on turnover of HK$15.6 million.
The domestic A share index lost 5.09 points or 1.26 percent to 398.74 on turnover of 2.6 billion yuan.
"The B share index was mainly fuelled by strong gains in Chongqing Chang'an," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said. "The company released better than expected interim results."
Chang'an Automobile, one of China's biggest mini-car makers, posted net profits on Saturday of 125.91 million yuan for the first half of 1997, up 41 percent from the year-ago period.
The counter was the morning's biggest gainer, rising HK$0.31 or 9.87 percent to HK$3.45 on volume of 360,200 shares, one of the most actively traded issues.
Gains in Bengang Steel also helped to lift the B share index, the Guotai analyst said. "Some investors thought the issue was under-valued and bought it as long-term investment."
Bengang Steel was up HK$0.12 to HK$2.22 on the session's heaviest volume of 840,500 shares. The issue has been moving below its offer price of HK$2.38 since its debut last month.
"Falls in A shares have failed to have an impact on B shares," an analyst at Everbright Securities said. "The B share index has very limited downside."
Analysts expected the B share index to advance further in the afternoon.
In the A share market, Fuzhou Tianyu Electric was the biggest loser, sliding a 10 percent limit-down to 1.48 yuan to 13.32 yuan on volume of 265,600 shares.
Brokers said the firm's release of worse-than-expected 1997 interim results helped to triggered a sell-off of its shares.
The A share market was in the middle of a consolidation phase and further losses were expected, brokers said.
